# odyssey-055 review (Odyssey 11.435–537)

Two passes over `units.json`, plus one pass over `gloss.json` (pass two). `t` was not touched (checked by script: the units still reproduce the edition). Counts by severity: **High 3, Medium 10, Low 19** (32 changes). Severity: High = the file would fail the validator or a speech is mis-marked; Medium = a grammatical label, a claim about a line, or a sense that was false or lost; Low = typography, house consistency, clarity.

## Findings for the caller (not fixable in this part)

1. **Quotation glyph clash at 463–464.** Validator rule 6 requires identical English for the two shipped half-lines, which carry double “ ” (odyssey-018 and -021 treat those speeches as top-level). In 055 the outer speech from 9.2 is open, so the rule would give ‘ ’. Shipped as “ ” to pass the validator. If the validator is relaxed to ignore quotation glyphs, change both to ‘ ’ and ’ (units at ln 463 first, and 464).
2. **odyssey-054 ends with Agamemnon’s speech (405–434) unclosed.** The last unit (ln 432, l and i) has no closing ’. It cannot be repaired from 055, because the first unit of 055 is the shipped formula. Fix in 054 if wanted.

## Considered and refused

- Capital letter after a semicolon in i (units at 438, 450, 481, 508, 512, 528): the shipped parts do both (054: 13 capitals, 19 lower-case after ; : ,). Left.
- 454 i “lay it up in your own mind”: an ordinary English idiom for ἐνὶ φρεσὶ βάλλεο; left.
- 457 i “whether you have heard” for present ἀκούετε: the glossary already gives “perfect force”; left.
- 505 i “your dear son Neoptolemus”: built from παιδός, φίλοιο; the note says the Greek has no ‘your’; left.
- 534 i ‘as so often happens in war’: assembled from the Greek, no fixed phrase recognised; left.
- 445 note “as it stands in the same line elsewhere in the poem” (περίφρων Πηνελόπεια): shown by the packet (odyssey-004), allowed; left.
- gloss `βιόωνται` “pres. 3 pl. mid.” does not name the mood (subjunctive or indicative -όωνται is uncertain); no false claim, left. `πέφνε`, `πέφνον` under θείνω agree with the shipped ἔπεφνεν entry. `πινυτή` glossed “discerning, prudent”: a dictionary gloss, not a rendering; left.
- Scansion: the packet flags none. A script scan finds no unresolved or ambiguous line; the six spondaic fifths (460, 496, 499, 500, 518, 528) and the lengthening at 478 and 530 are ordinary licences, so no metrical sentence was added to any note.
- new-renderings.md: only the παραυδάω row changed; every other row was checked against the units (ἀφραδής, πινυτός, φέρτατος, Ἀργεῖοι, εὐρύς, νήπιος, ἀσκηθής, χαλκοβαρές, δηιοτής, ἀάπτους, στύξαιμι, ἐπάρουρος, ἄκληρος, ἐπιμίξ, Κήτειοι, ποδώκης Αἰακίδης, Πηληϊάδης) and agrees.

## Checks run

Units reproduce the edition; l has one `\n` per `\n` of t; i has none; whole-unit repeats match shipped English (rule 6 simulated against all published parts: no mismatch); every speech opens with ‘ (or “ at 463) on its first unit and closes on its last; marks and `p` flags match Murray’s paragraphs (435, 440, 462, 465, 473, 477, 487, 504); note lengths 20–130 words; no ASCII apostrophe or backtick in notes; gloss.json covers every form not already in the glossary, every entry has the `lemma — meaning; parse` shape, and every broadening extends the old entry whole. The full validator was not run, because no built odyssey-055.json exists.
